home.summary: The home is inviolable and private property is guaranteed by the Constitution.

properties.explanation: No one may enter a home without the occupant's consent, except with a court's permission or to stop a crime under way or in an emergency.

items.text: The home is inviolable. No one may enter or stay in it without its occupant's consent, except in the cases expressly specified by law.

Entering or staying in a home without its occupant's consent or without the permission of the judiciary is allowed only to prevent a crime that is imminent or under way, to catch its perpetrator, or in cases of extreme necessity.

text: (1) In pre-trial proceedings, search and seizure are carried out with the permission of a judge of the competent first-instance court, or of the first-instance court in whose area the action is taken, at the prosecutor's request.

(2) In urgent cases, when it is the only way to gather and preserve evidence, the pre-trial authorities may search and seize without that permission; the prosecutor must then submit the record to the judge for approval immediately, and no later than 24 hours.

properties.explanation: Private and family life, and correspondence, are protected; exceptions need a court's permission.

items.text: The private life of citizens is inviolable. Everyone has the right to protection against unlawful interference in their private and family life and against attacks on their honour, dignity and good name.

text: (1) The freedom and secrecy of correspondence and other communications are inviolable.
(2) Exceptions are allowed only with the permission of the judiciary, when needed to detect or prevent serious crimes.

properties.explanation: Private property, including the home, is inviolable; expropriation only by law and with prior equivalent compensation.

text: (1) The right of property and of inheritance is guaranteed and protected by law.
(2) Property is private and public.
(3) Private property is inviolable.

properties.explanation: Raising children is the parents' right and duty, and only a court can restrict or remove parental rights. But social services can take a child from the family by administrative order and have a month before they must go to court.

items.text: Raising and bringing up children until they come of age is the right and the duty of their parents and is supported by the state.
The conditions and procedure for restricting or removing parental rights are set by law.

text: (1) The parent has the right and duty to care for the child's physical, mental, moral and social development, its education, and its personal and property interests.

(2) The parent raises the child, shapes its views and provides for its education according to the parent's means and the child's needs and inclinations, with the aim of its growing into an independent and responsible person. The parent may not use violence or methods of upbringing that degrade the child's dignity.

items.text: When a parent's conduct endangers the child's person, health, upbringing or property, the district court takes appropriate measures in the child's interest, restricting parental rights by removing some of them or setting conditions on their exercise, and may assign them to another person. Where needed, the child's residence may be changed or the child placed outside the family.

text: A parent may be deprived of parental rights:
1. in particularly serious cases under Article 131;
2. when, without good reason, the parent persistently fails to care for and support the child.

items.text: Placement of a child with relatives or friends, in a foster family, or in a residential social or integrated health-social service is ordered by the court. Until the court rules, the Social Assistance Directorate at the child's current address makes a temporary placement by administrative order.
Within one month of the order under paragraph 1, the Social Assistance Directorate applies to the district court.
items.fix: Within three days of the order under paragraph 1, the Social Assistance Directorate applies to the district court, which rules within seven days. If the court does not confirm the placement, the order lapses and the child returns to the family.
items.why: No child stays away from the parents for more than a few days without a judge's decision.

properties.explanation: Spouses, and both parents, decide family matters together and as equals; a court settles only disputes they bring to it.

items.text: Relations between spouses are built on mutual respect, shared care for the family, and understanding.

Spouses are obliged, by mutual understanding and joint effort and according to their abilities, property and income, to secure the family's well-being and to care for the raising, upbringing, education and support of the children.

text: (1) Each parent holds parental rights and duties regarding children who are minors.
(2) Parents have equal rights and duties whether or not they are married.
(1) Parental rights and duties are exercised in the child's interest by both parents, together and separately. A parent who acted alone must inform the other parent.

(2) Parental rights and duties are exercised by mutual agreement of the parents. If they disagree, they may turn to a mediator or bring a claim before the district court at the child's current address, which settles the dispute after hearing the parents and, where necessary, the child.

properties.explanation: A child has the right to a normal development, and can turn to social services or, from 14, a court. Placement outside the family is a last resort ordered by a court; social services may place a child temporarily only until the court rules, within a month.

text: (1) The child has the right to be raised and brought up in a way that ensures its normal physical, mental, moral and social development.

(3) If a parent and child disagree, the child may personally ask the Social Assistance Directorate for help. If the child is 14 or older and the disagreement is on essential matters, it may, through the directorate, take the dispute to the district court.

items.text: Placement outside the family is imposed as a protection measure only after all possibilities for protection within the family are exhausted, except where the child must be removed urgently.

Placement of a child with relatives or friends, in a foster family, or in a residential social or integrated health-social service is ordered by the court. Until the court rules, the Social Assistance Directorate at the child's current address makes a temporary placement by administrative order.
Within one month of the order under paragraph 1, the Social Assistance Directorate applies to the district court.

text: Police protection is an emergency measure taken when the child is:
1. the object of crimes or in immediate danger to its life or health, or at risk of being drawn into crime;
2. lost or helpless;
3. left without supervision.

properties.explanation: Victims of domestic violence can get a court order, including removing the abuser from the shared home.

text: (1) Domestic violence is any act of physical, sexual, psychological or economic violence, or an attempt at it, and any forced restriction of private life, personal freedom or personal rights, committed against persons who are related, who are or were in a family relationship, de facto marital cohabitation, or an intimate relationship.
(2) Any domestic violence committed in a child's presence also counts as psychological violence against the child.
The protection measures are:
1. ordering the perpetrator to refrain from domestic violence;
2. removing the perpetrator from the shared home for a period set by the court;
3. barring the perpetrator from approaching the victim, their home, workplace and places of social contact and recreation;
4. barring any contact with the victim;
5. temporarily setting the child's residence with the victim parent.

properties.explanation: School is compulsory to 16. Parents can educate at home only in the self-study form, and only after a regional expert commission approves it, with checks every term in which a social-assistance representative must take part.

items.text: School education is compulsory until age 16 and begins in the school year starting in the year the child turns 7.

text: The self-study form is open to:
2. pupils of compulsory school age, at the pupil's or parent's wish, under Article 12(2).

items.text: For the pupils under paragraph 1, item 2, the self-study form is organised after a decision of an expert commission set up at the Regional Education Office.
items.fix: For the pupils under paragraph 1, item 2, the self-study form is organised on the parents' written notification to the school.
items.why: Parents may choose home education by notifying the school, without a commission's approval.

items.text: Control is exercised every school term by the expert commission. A representative of the Social Assistance Agency must take part in the commission.
items.fix: The pupil's progress is assessed through the annual exams under paragraph 3.
items.why: Drops the termly checks and the social-assistance representative; the annual exams remain.

representative.note: The people in a home decide for themselves; representation does not apply.

individual.summary: Personal autonomy is protected by the Constitution.

properties.explanation: Property is guaranteed and private property is inviolable; privacy and the home are inviolable.
These rights can be restricted by statute on the grounds the Constitution allows, e.g. entry into a home with consent or by court order.

representative.note: Individuals decide for themselves; representation does not apply.

business.summary: People can start a business and govern it themselves through the owners' meeting and the managers they elect.

properties.explanation: The Constitution bases the economy on free economic initiative: anyone may start and run a business.

items.text: The economy of the Republic of Bulgaria shall be based on free economic initiative.

The state shall establish and guarantee equal legal conditions for economic activity to all citizens and corporate entities by preventing any abuse of a monopoly status and unfair competition, and by protecting the consumer.
All investments and economic activity by Bulgarian and foreign persons and corporate entities shall enjoy the protection of the law.

properties.explanation: An authority's licence or permit is a condition for starting many activities, so an outsider decides whether one may trade at all. The law allows licences only for activities that concern state property or create an increased risk to security, public order, people's rights or the environment, and only when set by an act of parliament.

text: State and local authorities regulate and control economic activity administratively in order to protect:
1. national security and public order in the Republic of Bulgaria, and the exclusive and sovereign rights of the state under Article 18(1)–(4) of the Constitution;
2. the personal and property rights of citizens and legal persons;
3. the environment.

items.text: In regulating and controlling economic activity, administrative and local authorities may not impose restrictions and burdens that are not necessary to achieve the aims of the law.

Licensing and registration regimes for carrying out economic activity, and any requirement to obtain a permit or certificate or to give notice of a single transaction or act, are established only by law.

text: A licensing regime may be established only for economic activities that:
1. concern objects that are exclusive state property under Article 18(1) of the Constitution, or objects over which the state exercises sovereign rights; or

2. create an increased risk to national security or public order in the Republic of Bulgaria, to the personal or property rights of citizens or the rights of legal persons, or to the environment, and are listed in the annex to this Act.

items.text: Holding a licence is a condition for starting and lawfully carrying out the economic activity concerned.

properties.explanation: The parties may freely set the content of their contract, within the mandatory rules of the law and good morals, and the contract binds them like a law.

items.text: The parties may freely determine the content of the contract, insofar as it does not contradict the mandatory rules of the law and good morals.

text: (1) Contracts have the force of law for those who concluded them.
(2) Contracts may be amended, terminated, rescinded or revoked only by mutual consent of the parties or on grounds provided by law.

properties.explanation: The state fixes some terms whatever both parties want: the Council of Ministers sets the minimum wage, and the energy and water regulator sets the prices of district heating, gas for households, and water and sewerage. Rules against fraud and coercion, and against unfair terms a consumer could not negotiate, protect the parties' own consent, so they are not counted.

items.text: Contracts that contradict or circumvent the law, as well as contracts that offend good morals, including contracts on inheritances not yet opened, are void.

text: The Council of Ministers determines:
1. the national minimum wage for each calendar year;
2. the types and minimum amounts of additional pay and of compensation under the employment relationship, insofar as they are not set by this Code.

items.text: The national minimum wage set under paragraph 2 may not be lower than the one set for the previous year.
Higher minimum wages may be agreed in collective labour agreements at sector and branch level.

text: The following prices are subject to regulation by the Commission:
3. at which producers sell heat to the heat transmission company and to directly connected customers;
4. at which the heat transmission company sells heat to customers;
8. at which end suppliers sell natural gas to customers connected to the gas distribution networks;
The following prices at which water and sewerage operators provide services are subject to regulation by the Commission:
1. supplying water to consumers;
2. removing waste water;
3. treating waste water;
4. connecting consumers to the water supply systems;
5. connecting consumers to the sewerage systems.

properties.explanation: Partners in a general or limited partnership (СД, КД) or a limited liability company (ООД) decide in a general meeting.
Its resolutions bind the company.
Owners decide the company's statutes, profits and leadership.
The partnership or company controls its own capital and income.
Shareholders of a joint-stock company (АД) or partnership limited by shares (КДА) decide in a general meeting.
Its resolutions bind the company.
Owners decide the company's statutes, profits and leadership.
The company controls its own capital and income.
Members of a cooperative decide in its general meeting, one member one vote.
Its resolutions bind the company.
Members decide the statutes, the use of any surplus and the board.
The cooperative controls its own capital and income.
Owners elect the managers or board.
Managers and board members are elected individually.
The owners can dismiss them.
Anyone may authorise another person to act for them by a power of attorney or a mandate contract; a merchant may appoint a procurator (прокурист) or a commercial agent.
The principal chooses the agent.
The principal may revoke the power of attorney or the mandate at any time.
The agent must report and hand over everything received for the principal.
The agent must act in the principal's interest; a procurator may not compete with the merchant.
Bulgaria has no trusts. Only licensed investment firms and fund management companies may manage assets for others.
A client chooses their portfolio manager, but a fund's investors do not choose its management company.
A client can end a portfolio management contract; a fund's investors can only leave by redeeming their units.
Managers must report regularly to clients and investors.
Managers must act in the clients' best interest and manage conflicts of interest.

nonprofit.summary: People can form non-profit associations and foundations and govern them through a members' assembly and an elected board.

properties.explanation: People may freely form associations and foundations.
Registration and, for public-benefit status, supervision by the state.
Members decide in a general assembly.
Its decisions bind the organisation.
Members adopt the statutes and elect the board.
Funded by members, donors and grants; tax relief depends on public-benefit status.
The members elect a board.
The members can dismiss the board.

entrance.summary: Owners can organise a condominium per entrance, with a general assembly of owners and an elected management board. Quorum is low and falls to zero on the next day.

properties.explanation: Where a building has more than one entrance, it can be managed separately for each entrance.
Decisions of the general assembly bind owners, users and occupants, including new ones.
51% of ideal shares must be present; after one hour 26% suffice; if still not, the meeting is held the next day with whoever attends.
Owners holding at least 20% of the ideal shares can require the meeting to be convened.
The assembly adopts the house rules, budget, contributions, the repair plan, loans and the use of common areas.
The assembly sets the contributions to the repair and renovation fund.
The executive body is a management board or a single manager.
The board implements the assembly's decisions and manages the common parts.
Board members are elected individually by the general assembly.
The term is up to two years, and the general assembly can end it early for failure to perform.

building.summary: Same regime as for an entrance: the Condominium Management Act applies to the building, or separately to each entrance.

neighbourhood.summary: A district (район) can hold a citizen-initiated local referendum; a smaller quarter (квартал) that is not a district or кметство cannot. A general assembly is possible but needs one quarter of residents to attend and is not directly binding. Municipal councillors are elected from municipality-wide party lists, so no councillor answers to the quarter.

properties.explanation: A local referendum can be held for a district (район) of Sofia, Plovdiv or Varna, as well as for a municipality or кметство.

text: Direct participation shall be exercised through:
1. a referendum;

items.ref: Chapter II – Referendum, Section III – Local referendum

items.text: A local referendum shall be held in a municipality, district (район) or mayoralty (кметство) to decide directly on matters of local importance that the law has placed within the competence of the bodies of local self-government or of the bodies of the district or mayoralty.

properties.explanation: The decision needs no later approval by the municipal council; it takes effect when announced and the mayor organises its implementation.

items.text: A decision adopted by local referendum shall not be subject to subsequent approval by the municipal council. The council shall adopt an act where necessary for its implementation.
A decision adopted by local referendum shall enter into force immediately upon its announcement.
The implementation of a decision adopted by local referendum shall be organised by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty.

properties.explanation: Held on its own, a local referendum needs at least 40% turnout (a participation quorum). Held together with local elections, it needs “yes” votes from more than half of those voting in the council election instead (an approval quorum), which is less fatal. But whether it is held with the elections is up to the municipal council, which sets the date.

items.text: The proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if no fewer than 40 per cent of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality have taken part in it and more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.
items.fix: The proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.
items.why: Removes the 40% turnout quorum: the majority of those who vote decides.

items.text: When the referendum is held at the same time as general elections for municipal councillors and mayors, the proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the valid votes cast in the respective municipality in the elections for municipal councillors have answered “yes”.
items.fix: When the referendum is held at the same time as general elections for municipal councillors and mayors, the proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.
items.why: Removes the approval quorum tied to the number of election voters.

items.text: The municipal council shall set the date for holding the referendum no earlier than 45 days and no later than 60 days after the decision on the referendum.
The municipal council shall set the date of voting on a non-working day. When several proposals have been received, the municipal council shall set a common date for holding the local referendum.

properties.explanation: Voters answer a question with yes or no; they do not vote on a drafted text such as an ordinance or a law.

items.text: When a local referendum is held, voting may be on one or on several questions.
items.fix: When a local referendum is held, voting may be on one or on several questions, or on a draft decision, ordinance or other act within the competence of the municipal council, which, if approved, takes effect as worded.
items.why: Lets voters approve a drafted decision or ordinance, which then takes effect as worded.

properties.explanation: 1/20 of voters to propose. The council is obliged to call it only with 1/10 of voters, which in Sofia means well over 100,000 signatures.

text: A local referendum shall be held on the proposal of:

3. an initiative committee with the signatures of no fewer than one twentieth of the citizens with voting rights who have a permanent address in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty at the time the proposal is entered in the register.
fix: A local referendum shall be held on the proposal of:

3. an initiative committee with the signatures of no fewer than one hundredth of the citizens with voting rights who have a permanent address in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty at the time the proposal is entered in the register.
items.why: Lowers the signatures needed to propose a local referendum from 1/20 to 1/100 of voters.

items.text: The municipal council shall adopt a decision to hold a local referendum when this has been requested by an initiative committee with a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than one tenth of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty, and it does not contravene the restriction under Article 26(2).
items.fix: The municipal council shall adopt a decision to hold a local referendum when this has been requested by an initiative committee with a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than one fiftieth of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty.
items.why: Lowers the signatures that oblige the council to call it from 1/10 to 1/50 of voters, and drops the topic restriction.

items.text: If the petition is not submitted to the municipal council within three months of notifying it, the procedure for submitting a proposal for a referendum shall be terminated by the chairperson of the municipal council.
items.fix: If the petition is not submitted to the municipal council within six months of notifying it, the procedure for submitting a proposal for a referendum shall be terminated by the chairperson of the municipal council.
items.why: Gives the initiative committee six months instead of three to collect signatures.

properties.explanation: The municipal budget, the size of local taxes and fees, and the council’s internal rules cannot be put to a local referendum.

text: The following questions may not be decided by local referendum:
1. the municipal budget;
2. the size of local taxes and fees;
3. the rules of the internal organisation and activity of the municipal council.
fix: (repealed)
items.why: Lifts the ban on local referendums about the budget, local taxes and fees, and the council's rules.

properties.explanation: If the council's term ends before it decides on a petition, the law does not say the procedure continues before the next council, so the petition can lapse.

items.fix: If the term of office of the municipal council ends before it has decided on a petition submitted under Article 27(2), the procedure shall continue before the newly elected council, which shall decide on the petition within one month of its first session.
items.why: A petition no longer lapses when the council's term ends.

properties.explanation: A veto referendum exists only for the whole municipality (Art. 27(3)); a village or quarter cannot veto a decision that concerns only it.

items.fix: When a decision of the municipal council concerns only one district, mayoralty or quarter, the procedure under paragraph 3 may be initiated with the signatures of one fiftieth of the citizens with voting rights there, and the referendum shall be held in that district, mayoralty or quarter.
items.why: Lets a district, village or quarter veto a council decision that concerns only it.

properties.explanation: The law does not provide this kind of referendum.

items.fix: Decisions of the municipal council on new non-recurring expenditure exceeding 5 per cent of the annual budget, on long-term municipal debt, and on the disposal of municipal property of public importance shall take effect only after their approval by local referendum. When such a decision concerns only one district, mayoralty or quarter, the referendum shall be held there.
items.why: Sends large spending, debt and sales of public property to the voters automatically.

mechanisms.name: General assembly of the population (общо събрание на населението)

properties.explanation: Only quarters (квартали) and districts of up to 10,000 inhabitants can hold one, which rules out most city neighbourhoods.

text: Direct participation shall be exercised through:
4. a general assembly of the population.

items.ref: Chapter IV – General assembly of the population

items.text: A general assembly of the population shall be held to decide matters of local importance which, on grounds of expediency, fall within the competence of the respective municipal council or mayor.
A general assembly of the population shall be held in municipalities, districts, mayoralties, settlements and quarters with a population of up to 10,000 inhabitants.
items.fix: A general assembly of the population shall be held in municipalities, districts, mayoralties, settlements and quarters.
items.why: Removes the 10,000-inhabitant limit on general assemblies.

properties.explanation: Binding in effect. Within 7 days the mayor must either order the measures that implement the decision or, where it needs a council act, propose one; the council or mayor must issue the implementing acts within a month (Art. 54, 63(3)).

items.text: The municipal council or the mayor of the municipality shall be obliged to issue the relevant acts to take the necessary action within one month of the adoption of the decision of the general assembly of the population in the municipality, district or mayoralty, unless the general assembly itself has set a longer period.
The municipal council shall take the necessary action within one month of the adoption of the decision of the general assembly of the population in the settlement or quarter.

On the basis of the decision of the general assembly, the mayor shall, within 7 days, issue an order specifying the measures for its implementation, or submit a proposal to the municipal council for the preparation and adoption of a relevant decision, rules or ordinance.

properties.explanation: One quarter of eligible voters must attend (one third in places of up to 150 inhabitants). If not, after one hour it may proceed only with one tenth. In a quarter of 10,000 that is 1,000 people in one room.

items.text: The general assembly of the population shall be deemed quorate if no fewer than one quarter of the citizens with voting rights in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter are present.
items.fix: The general assembly of the population shall be deemed quorate whatever the number of citizens with voting rights present, provided it has been convened and announced as this Act requires.
items.why: Removes the attendance quorum: those who come decide.

items.text: In settlements with up to 150 inhabitants, at least one third of the citizens with voting rights in the settlement must be present for a general assembly of the population to be held.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Removes the stricter quorum for small settlements.

items.text: If the required number of citizens has not appeared at the set time, the assembly shall be postponed by one hour, after which it shall be held with those present. Their number, however, may not be less than one tenth of all citizens with voting rights.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Removes the fallback quorum of one tenth.

properties.explanation: The mayor must convene it on request of 1/50 of eligible voters, at least 20 people.

text: The general assembly of the population shall be convened by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty on:

3. the request of at least one fiftieth, but no fewer than 20, citizens with voting rights with a permanent or current address in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter at the time the request is made.

items.text: The initiative committee shall submit the petition to the mayor, who shall be obliged to convene the general assembly of the population within the period stated in it.
The general assembly shall be held no earlier than 15 days and no later than one month after it has been announced.

properties.explanation: 1/50 of voters, at least 20 people.

text: The general assembly of the population shall be convened by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty on:

3. the request of at least one fiftieth, but no fewer than 20, citizens with voting rights with a permanent or current address in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter at the time the request is made.

properties.explanation: The law provides no elected body for a neighbourhood (квартал). Districts (райони) of Sofia, Plovdiv and Varna elect only a district mayor, who carries out municipal decisions; there are no district councils.

items.text: The constituent administrative-territorial units within municipalities are mayoralties (кметства) and districts (райони). They are created under conditions and by a procedure laid down by law.
items.fix: The constituent administrative-territorial units within municipalities are mayoralties (кметства), districts (райони) and quarters (квартали). They are created under conditions and by a procedure laid down by law.
items.why: Makes quarters units of local self-government.

items.text: Mayors of districts are elected in the districts of Sofia Municipality and of cities divided into districts.
items.fix: Mayors and councils of districts are elected in the districts of Sofia Municipality and of cities divided into districts. Quarter councils are elected in quarters.
items.why: Gives districts and quarters elected councils of their own.

text: The mayor of a district or mayoralty:
1. implements the municipal budget in its part for the district or mayoralty;
2. organises improvement, communal and other activities;
3. is responsible for managing municipal property sites designated by the municipal council;
11. organises the implementation of the acts of the municipal council and of the mayor of the municipality relating to the territory and citizens of the district or mayoralty;
12. performs functions assigned by the mayor of the municipality.
fix: The mayor of a district or mayoralty:
1. implements the budget of the district or mayoralty adopted by its council;
2. organises improvement, communal and other activities;
3. manages the municipal property located in the district or mayoralty and serving its residents;

11. organises the implementation of the acts of the council of the district or mayoralty, and of the acts of the municipal council and of the mayor of the municipality on matters of municipal importance;
12. (repealed)
items.why: The district or mayoralty mayor implements its own council's decisions and budget.

mechanisms.name: Own member of the municipal council

properties.explanation: The whole municipality is one constituency, so no councillor is elected by, or answers to, the neighbourhood.

items.text: For elections for municipal councillors, the territory of the municipality constitutes one multi-member constituency.
items.fix: For elections for municipal councillors, the territory of the municipality is divided into constituencies of three to five seats each, which follow the boundaries of its districts, mayoralties and quarters.
items.why: Splits the municipality into districts of 3 to 5 seats along districts, mayoralties and quarters.

items.text: The results of the voting for municipal councillors under the proportional system are determined by the Hare-Niemeyer method.
items.fix: The results of the voting for municipal councillors are determined by the single transferable vote.
items.why: Replaces the Hare-Niemeyer list count with STV.

village.summary: A village that is a кметство elects its own mayor and can hold a local referendum, but has no council and no budget of its own. In smaller villages the municipal mayor appoints a deputy (кметски наместник) instead.

properties.explanation: A local referendum can be held for a кметство.

text: Direct participation shall be exercised through:
1. a referendum;

items.ref: Chapter II – Referendum, Section III – Local referendum

items.text: A local referendum shall be held in a municipality, district (район) or mayoralty (кметство) to decide directly on matters of local importance that the law has placed within the competence of the bodies of local self-government or of the bodies of the district or mayoralty.

properties.explanation: The decision needs no later approval by the municipal council; it takes effect when announced and the mayor organises its implementation.

items.text: A decision adopted by local referendum shall not be subject to subsequent approval by the municipal council. The council shall adopt an act where necessary for its implementation.
A decision adopted by local referendum shall enter into force immediately upon its announcement.
The implementation of a decision adopted by local referendum shall be organised by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty.

properties.explanation: Held on its own, a local referendum needs at least 40% turnout (a participation quorum). Held together with local elections, it needs “yes” votes from more than half of those voting in the council election instead (an approval quorum), which is less fatal. But whether it is held with the elections is up to the municipal council, which sets the date.

items.text: The proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if no fewer than 40 per cent of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality have taken part in it and more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.
items.fix: The proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.
items.why: Removes the 40% turnout quorum: the majority of those who vote decides.

items.text: When the referendum is held at the same time as general elections for municipal councillors and mayors, the proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the valid votes cast in the respective municipality in the elections for municipal councillors have answered “yes”.
items.fix: When the referendum is held at the same time as general elections for municipal councillors and mayors, the proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have answered “yes”.
items.why: Removes the approval quorum tied to the number of election voters.

items.text: The municipal council shall set the date for holding the referendum no earlier than 45 days and no later than 60 days after the decision on the referendum.
The municipal council shall set the date of voting on a non-working day. When several proposals have been received, the municipal council shall set a common date for holding the local referendum.

properties.explanation: Voters answer a question with yes or no; they do not vote on a drafted text such as an ordinance or a law.

items.text: When a local referendum is held, voting may be on one or on several questions.
items.fix: When a local referendum is held, voting may be on one or on several questions, or on a draft decision, ordinance or other act within the competence of the municipal council, which, if approved, takes effect as worded.
items.why: Lets voters approve a drafted decision or ordinance, which then takes effect as worded.

properties.explanation: 1/20 of voters to propose. The council is obliged to call it only with 1/10 of voters, which in Sofia means well over 100,000 signatures.

text: A local referendum shall be held on the proposal of:

3. an initiative committee with the signatures of no fewer than one twentieth of the citizens with voting rights who have a permanent address in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty at the time the proposal is entered in the register.
fix: A local referendum shall be held on the proposal of:

3. an initiative committee with the signatures of no fewer than one hundredth of the citizens with voting rights who have a permanent address in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty at the time the proposal is entered in the register.
items.why: Lowers the signatures needed to propose a local referendum from 1/20 to 1/100 of voters.

items.text: The municipal council shall adopt a decision to hold a local referendum when this has been requested by an initiative committee with a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than one tenth of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty, and it does not contravene the restriction under Article 26(2).
items.fix: The municipal council shall adopt a decision to hold a local referendum when this has been requested by an initiative committee with a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than one fiftieth of the citizens with voting rights in the respective municipality, district or mayoralty.
items.why: Lowers the signatures that oblige the council to call it from 1/10 to 1/50 of voters, and drops the topic restriction.

items.text: If the petition is not submitted to the municipal council within three months of notifying it, the procedure for submitting a proposal for a referendum shall be terminated by the chairperson of the municipal council.
items.fix: If the petition is not submitted to the municipal council within six months of notifying it, the procedure for submitting a proposal for a referendum shall be terminated by the chairperson of the municipal council.
items.why: Gives the initiative committee six months instead of three to collect signatures.

properties.explanation: The municipal budget, the size of local taxes and fees, and the council’s internal rules cannot be put to a local referendum.

text: The following questions may not be decided by local referendum:
1. the municipal budget;
2. the size of local taxes and fees;
3. the rules of the internal organisation and activity of the municipal council.
fix: (repealed)
items.why: Lifts the ban on local referendums about the budget, local taxes and fees, and the council's rules.

properties.explanation: If the council's term ends before it decides on a petition, the law does not say the procedure continues before the next council, so the petition can lapse.

items.fix: If the term of office of the municipal council ends before it has decided on a petition submitted under Article 27(2), the procedure shall continue before the newly elected council, which shall decide on the petition within one month of its first session.
items.why: A petition no longer lapses when the council's term ends.

properties.explanation: A veto referendum exists only for the whole municipality (Art. 27(3)); a village or quarter cannot veto a decision that concerns only it.

items.fix: When a decision of the municipal council concerns only one district, mayoralty or quarter, the procedure under paragraph 3 may be initiated with the signatures of one fiftieth of the citizens with voting rights there, and the referendum shall be held in that district, mayoralty or quarter.
items.why: Lets a district, village or quarter veto a council decision that concerns only it.

properties.explanation: The law does not require any decision to go to a vote automatically.

items.fix: Decisions of the municipal council on new non-recurring expenditure exceeding 5 per cent of the annual budget, on long-term municipal debt, and on the disposal of municipal property of public importance shall take effect only after their approval by local referendum. When such a decision concerns only one district, mayoralty or quarter, the referendum shall be held there.
items.why: Sends large spending, debt and sales of public property to the voters automatically.

mechanisms.name: General assembly of the population (общо събрание на населението)

populationRule.unknownNote: Villages in Bulgaria have well under 10,000 inhabitants, so a general assembly can be held.

properties.explanation: Can be held for a settlement or кметство, including residential areas (квартали) of up to 10,000 inhabitants.

text: Direct participation shall be exercised through:
4. a general assembly of the population.

items.ref: Chapter IV – General assembly of the population

items.text: A general assembly of the population shall be held to decide matters of local importance which, on grounds of expediency, fall within the competence of the respective municipal council or mayor.
A general assembly of the population shall be held in municipalities, districts, mayoralties, settlements and quarters with a population of up to 10,000 inhabitants.
items.fix: A general assembly of the population shall be held in municipalities, districts, mayoralties, settlements and quarters.
items.why: Removes the 10,000-inhabitant limit on general assemblies.

properties.explanation: Binding in effect. Within 7 days the mayor must either order the measures that implement the decision or, where it needs a council act, propose one; the council or mayor must issue the implementing acts within a month (Art. 54, 63(3)).

items.text: The municipal council or the mayor of the municipality shall be obliged to issue the relevant acts to take the necessary action within one month of the adoption of the decision of the general assembly of the population in the municipality, district or mayoralty, unless the general assembly itself has set a longer period.
The municipal council shall take the necessary action within one month of the adoption of the decision of the general assembly of the population in the settlement or quarter.

On the basis of the decision of the general assembly, the mayor shall, within 7 days, issue an order specifying the measures for its implementation, or submit a proposal to the municipal council for the preparation and adoption of a relevant decision, rules or ordinance.

properties.explanation: One quarter of eligible voters must attend (one third in places of up to 150 inhabitants). If not, after one hour it may proceed only with one tenth. In a quarter of 10,000 that is 1,000 people in one room.

items.text: The general assembly of the population shall be deemed quorate if no fewer than one quarter of the citizens with voting rights in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter are present.
items.fix: The general assembly of the population shall be deemed quorate whatever the number of citizens with voting rights present, provided it has been convened and announced as this Act requires.
items.why: Removes the attendance quorum: those who come decide.

items.text: In settlements with up to 150 inhabitants, at least one third of the citizens with voting rights in the settlement must be present for a general assembly of the population to be held.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Removes the stricter quorum for small settlements.

items.text: If the required number of citizens has not appeared at the set time, the assembly shall be postponed by one hour, after which it shall be held with those present. Their number, however, may not be less than one tenth of all citizens with voting rights.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Removes the fallback quorum of one tenth.

properties.explanation: The mayor must convene it on request of 1/50 of eligible voters, at least 20 people.

text: The general assembly of the population shall be convened by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty on:

3. the request of at least one fiftieth, but no fewer than 20, citizens with voting rights with a permanent or current address in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter at the time the request is made.

items.text: The initiative committee shall submit the petition to the mayor, who shall be obliged to convene the general assembly of the population within the period stated in it.
The general assembly shall be held no earlier than 15 days and no later than one month after it has been announced.

properties.explanation: 1/50 of voters, at least 20 people.

text: The general assembly of the population shall be convened by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty on:

3. the request of at least one fiftieth, but no fewer than 20, citizens with voting rights with a permanent or current address in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter at the time the request is made.

properties.explanation: Кметства elect only a mayor. There is no village council; the municipal council decides.

items.text: Municipal councils and mayors of municipalities are elected in municipalities.
Mayors of mayoralties are elected in mayoralties.
items.fix: Mayors and councils of mayoralties are elected in mayoralties.
items.why: Gives mayoralties an elected council of their own.

properties.explanation: A village of over 100 permanent residents is a mayoralty (кметство) and elects its own mayor. In smaller villages the municipal mayor may appoint a mayoral deputy (кметски наместник), who is not elected and can be dismissed without notice.

items.text: A mayoralty (кметство) is a settlement with a population of over 100 persons with a permanent address.
The territory of the mayoralty is the territory of the settlement.
Mayors of mayoralties are elected in mayoralties.
items.fix: Mayors and councils of mayoralties are elected in mayoralties.
items.why: Gives mayoralties an elected council of their own.

items.text: The mayor of the municipality, as well as the mayors of districts and mayoralties, are elected directly by the population for a term of 4 years under conditions and by a procedure laid down in the Electoral Code.

text: In settlements that are not the administrative centre of a mayoralty, the mayor of the municipality may appoint mayoral deputies (кметски наместници) for the term of office, in line with the approved staffing and structure of the municipal administration.
Mayoral deputies are bodies of executive power in the settlement. They may be dismissed early without notice by the mayor of the municipality.
fix: In settlements that are not the administrative centre of a mayoralty, the residents elect mayoral deputies (кметски наместници) for the term of office.
Mayoral deputies are bodies of executive power in the settlement. They may be dismissed early only on the grounds laid down by law.
items.why: Residents elect their mayoral deputy, who can no longer be dismissed at will.

items.text: In mayoralties, voters also have one vote for mayor of the mayoralty, if such an election is held.

populationRule.overNote: It is a mayoralty (кметство) and elects its own mayor.
populationRule.underNote: It is not a mayoralty: the municipal mayor may appoint a mayoral deputy (кметски наместник), who is not elected and can be dismissed without notice.

properties.explanation: The кметство mayor only carries out the municipal budget and the council’s and municipal mayor’s acts for the village, with an advisory vote in the council. The municipal council sets the mayor’s powers and decides the budget, fees, property and plans, so the village cannot govern most of its own interests. No own budget: the municipal council sets the кметство's budget figures.

text: The mayor of a district or mayoralty:
1. implements the municipal budget in its part for the district or mayoralty;
2. organises improvement, communal and other activities;
3. is responsible for managing municipal property sites designated by the municipal council;
11. organises the implementation of the acts of the municipal council and of the mayor of the municipality relating to the territory and citizens of the district or mayoralty;
12. performs functions assigned by the mayor of the municipality.
fix: The mayor of a district or mayoralty:
1. implements the budget of the district or mayoralty adopted by its council;
2. organises improvement, communal and other activities;
3. manages the municipal property located in the district or mayoralty and serving its residents;

11. organises the implementation of the acts of the council of the district or mayoralty, and of the acts of the municipal council and of the mayor of the municipality on matters of municipal importance;
12. (repealed)
items.why: The district or mayoralty mayor implements its own council's decisions and budget.

items.text: The mayor of a district and the mayor of a mayoralty may take part in the sessions of the municipal council in an advisory capacity. They must be heard when matters concerning the mayoralty or district are discussed.

text: The municipal council:

6. adopts and amends the annual budget of the municipality, including the figures for the districts, mayoralties and settlements with mayoral deputies, monitors its implementation and adopts the report on it;
7. sets the amount of local fees;

8. adopts decisions on the acquisition, management and disposal of municipal property and determines the specific powers of the mayor of the municipality and of the mayors of districts and mayoralties;
11. adopts decisions on the creation and approval of spatial development plans and their amendments for the territory of the municipality or parts of it;
23. decides other matters of local importance that are not within the exclusive competence of other bodies.
fix: The municipal council:

6. adopts and amends the annual budget of the municipality, monitors its implementation and adopts the report on it; the districts and mayoralties adopt their own budgets from the revenues assigned to them by law;
7. sets the amount of local fees;

8. adopts decisions on the acquisition, management and disposal of municipal property, except property located in a district or mayoralty and serving its residents, which is managed by that district or mayoralty;
11. adopts decisions on the creation and approval of spatial development plans and their amendments for the territory of the municipality or parts of it;
23. decides other matters of local importance that are not within the competence of districts, mayoralties or other bodies.
items.why: Leaves district and mayoralty budgets and property to their own bodies.

properties.explanation: Elected individually by a two-round majority vote.

items.text: Elections for mayors are held under a majoritarian electoral system, with candidate lists of parties and coalitions, or of initiative committees, registered in single-member constituencies.

text: The candidate who has received more than half of the valid votes is elected mayor.
If no candidate for mayor is elected in the first round, a second round is held no later than 7 days after the first, on a non-working day.
If more than two candidates were registered and none was elected, only the two who received the most valid votes may take part in the second round.
In the second round, the candidate who received the most valid votes is elected.

properties.explanation: One quarter of eligible voters must attend (one third in places of up to 150 inhabitants). If not, after one hour it may proceed only with one tenth. In a quarter of 10,000 that is 1,000 people in one room.

items.text: The general assembly of the population shall be deemed quorate if no fewer than one quarter of the citizens with voting rights in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter are present.
items.fix: The general assembly of the population shall be deemed quorate whatever the number of citizens with voting rights present, provided it has been convened and announced as this Act requires.
items.why: Removes the attendance quorum: those who come decide.

items.text: In settlements with up to 150 inhabitants, at least one third of the citizens with voting rights in the settlement must be present for a general assembly of the population to be held.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Removes the stricter quorum for small settlements.

items.text: If the required number of citizens has not appeared at the set time, the assembly shall be postponed by one hour, after which it shall be held with those present. Their number, however, may not be less than one tenth of all citizens with voting rights.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Removes the fallback quorum of one tenth.

properties.explanation: The mayor must convene it on request of 1/50 of eligible voters, at least 20 people.

text: The general assembly of the population shall be convened by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty on:

3. the request of at least one fiftieth, but no fewer than 20, citizens with voting rights with a permanent or current address in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter at the time the request is made.

items.text: The initiative committee shall submit the petition to the mayor, who shall be obliged to convene the general assembly of the population within the period stated in it.
The general assembly shall be held no earlier than 15 days and no later than one month after it has been announced.

properties.explanation: 1/50 of voters, at least 20 people.

text: The general assembly of the population shall be convened by the mayor of the municipality, district or mayoralty on:

3. the request of at least one fiftieth, but no fewer than 20, citizens with voting rights with a permanent or current address in the municipality, district, mayoralty, settlement or quarter at the time the request is made.

properties.explanation: Elected directly by the population for four years.

items.text: Municipal councils and mayors of municipalities are elected in municipalities.

The mayor of the municipality, as well as the mayors of districts and mayoralties, are elected directly by the population for a term of 4 years under conditions and by a procedure laid down in the Electoral Code.

properties.explanation: Limited powers over many local interests. It adopts the budget and sets local fees, but it can set local tax rates only within the limits fixed by national law, and it does not appoint school principals, for example.

text: The municipal council:

6. adopts and amends the annual budget of the municipality, including the figures for the districts, mayoralties and settlements with mayoral deputies, monitors its implementation and adopts the report on it;
7. sets the amount of local fees;

8. adopts decisions on the acquisition, management and disposal of municipal property and determines the specific powers of the mayor of the municipality and of the mayors of districts and mayoralties;
11. adopts decisions on the creation and approval of spatial development plans and their amendments for the territory of the municipality or parts of it;
23. decides other matters of local importance that are not within the exclusive competence of other bodies.
fix: The municipal council:

6. adopts and amends the annual budget of the municipality, monitors its implementation and adopts the report on it; the districts and mayoralties adopt their own budgets from the revenues assigned to them by law;
7. sets the amount of local fees;

8. adopts decisions on the acquisition, management and disposal of municipal property, except property located in a district or mayoralty and serving its residents, which is managed by that district or mayoralty;
11. adopts decisions on the creation and approval of spatial development plans and their amendments for the territory of the municipality or parts of it;
23. decides other matters of local importance that are not within the competence of districts, mayoralties or other bodies.
items.why: Leaves district and mayoralty budgets and property to their own bodies.

properties.explanation: Not met. Voters must first choose a party list, and a preference is optional. Only one preference is allowed, with no ranking as in the single transferable vote. A vote without a preference counts as a preference for the first candidate on the list, which, together with the 7% threshold, makes it almost impossible to replace that candidate.

items.text: When voting for the candidate list of a party or coalition, the voter may mark one preference for a candidate on the list, thereby expressing a preference as to the order of the candidates on the list voted for.
items.fix: When voting, the voter may rank as many candidates as they wish in order of preference, by marking 1, 2, 3 and so on beside their names, regardless of the party, coalition or committee that nominated them.
items.why: Lets voters rank council candidates of any party, instead of one preference within a list.

items.text: The vote is valid for the candidate list even if no preference has been marked for a candidate from the list of the party or coalition voted for.
items.fix: The vote is valid if at least one candidate has been marked with the number 1.
items.why: A vote counts for a person, not for a list.

items.text: Where the voter has not marked a preference for a candidate on the chosen candidate list, a preference is counted for the candidate placed first on the list.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Ends the rule that gives unmarked preferences to the list's first candidate.

items.text: Preferences for individual candidates are valid if the number of votes received for the candidate is no less than 7 per cent of the votes cast for the candidate list.
items.fix: Candidates are elected by the single transferable vote: each ballot counts for the voter's highest-ranked candidate who can still use it, and surplus and eliminated candidates' votes are transferred by the voters' next preferences until all seats are filled.
items.why: Replaces the 7% preference threshold with STV counting.

properties.explanation: The law lists the grounds for early termination of a mandate (resignation, incapacity, absences, etc.); recall by voters is not among them.
The whole municipality is one constituency, so no councillor is elected by, or answers to, a particular part of it.

items.text: For elections for municipal councillors, the territory of the municipality constitutes one multi-member constituency.
items.fix: For elections for municipal councillors, the territory of the municipality is divided into constituencies of three to five seats each, which follow the boundaries of its districts, mayoralties and quarters.
items.why: Splits the municipality into districts of 3 to 5 seats along districts, mayoralties and quarters.

items.text: The results of the voting for municipal councillors under the proportional system are determined by the Hare-Niemeyer method.
items.fix: The results of the voting for municipal councillors are determined by the single transferable vote.
items.why: Replaces the Hare-Niemeyer list count with STV.

properties.explanation: The mayor is the executive body of the municipality.

items.text: Municipal councils and mayors of municipalities are elected in municipalities.

The mayor of the municipality, as well as the mayors of districts and mayoralties, are elected directly by the population for a term of 4 years under conditions and by a procedure laid down in the Electoral Code.

properties.explanation: The mayor directs all executive activity of the municipality and carries out the budget.

text: The mayor of the municipality:
1. directs all executive activity of the municipality;
5. organises the implementation of the municipal budget;
7. organises the implementation of the acts of the municipal council and reports on their implementation to the council twice a year.

properties.explanation: Elected individually by a two-round majority vote: more than half of the votes in the first round, or a run-off between the top two.

items.text: Elections for mayors are held under a majoritarian electoral system, with candidate lists of parties and coalitions, or of initiative committees, registered in single-member constituencies.

text: The candidate who has received more than half of the valid votes is elected mayor.
If no candidate for mayor is elected in the first round, a second round is held no later than 7 days after the first, on a non-working day.
If more than two candidates were registered and none was elected, only the two who received the most valid votes may take part in the second round.
In the second round, the candidate who received the most valid votes is elected.

properties.explanation: The law lists the grounds for early termination of a mandate (resignation, incapacity, absences, etc.); recall by voters is not among them.

county.summary: Regions (области) are run by a governor appointed by the national government. Residents have no direct or representative means at this level.

properties.explanation: There is no referendum at the level of an oblast.

state.summary: Bulgaria is a unitary state; there is no state level.

country.summary: National referendums are binding and 400,000 signatures force one, but a high turnout threshold applies and taxes and the budget are excluded. Parliament is elected from party lists in 31 districts with a 7% preference threshold.

properties.explanation: The National Assembly decides to hold a national referendum.

text: Direct participation shall be exercised through:
1. a referendum;

properties.explanation: No later approval by parliament is needed; conflicting acts stop applying after three months.

items.text: A decision adopted by national referendum shall not be subject to subsequent approval by the National Assembly. The National Assembly shall adopt an act where necessary to implement the decision.

properties.explanation: Adopted only if turnout is at least that of the last parliamentary election. With over 20% turnout it is merely sent to parliament.

items.text: The proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if the number of voters participating is no lower than the number who participated in the most recent National Assembly elections and if more than half of the voters participating in the referendum have voted “yes”.
items.fix: The proposal submitted to referendum shall be deemed adopted if more than half of the voters participating in the referendum have voted “yes”.
items.why: Removes the turnout quorum: the majority of those who vote decides.

properties.explanation: Voters answer a question with yes or no; they do not vote on a drafted text such as an ordinance or a law.
400,000 is roughly 6–7% of registered voters.

text: A proposal to the National Assembly to hold a national referendum may be made by:
5. an initiative committee of citizens with voting rights that has collected no fewer than 200,000 signatures of citizens with voting rights.
fix: A proposal to the National Assembly to hold a national referendum may be made by:
5. an initiative committee of citizens with voting rights that has collected no fewer than 50,000 signatures of citizens with voting rights.
items.why: Lowers the signatures needed to propose a national referendum from 200,000 to 50,000.

items.text: The National Assembly shall adopt a decision to hold a national referendum when this has been requested by an initiative committee with a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than 400,000 Bulgarian citizens with voting rights, and it does not contravene the restrictions under Article 9(2), (3) and (4).
items.fix: The National Assembly shall adopt a decision to hold a national referendum when this has been requested by an initiative committee with a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than 100,000 Bulgarian citizens with voting rights.
items.why: Lowers the signatures that oblige parliament to call a referendum from 400,000 to 100,000, and drops the topic restrictions.

items.text: If the petition is not submitted to the National Assembly within three months of the notification under paragraph 2, item 3, the procedure for submitting a proposal for a referendum shall be terminated by the Chairperson of the National Assembly, and this shall be entered in the register under Article 10(3).
items.fix: If the petition is not submitted to the National Assembly within six months of the notification under paragraph 2, item 3, the procedure for submitting a proposal for a referendum shall be terminated by the Chairperson of the National Assembly, and this shall be entered in the register under Article 10(3).
items.why: Gives the initiative committee six months instead of three to collect signatures.

properties.explanation: The state budget, the size of taxes, fees and social security contributions, the National Assembly’s internal rules, a list of constitutional powers, and whole codes cannot be put to a national referendum.

text: The following questions may not be decided by national referendum:
1. (repealed)
2. those under Article 84, items 4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 16 and 17, Articles 91 and 91a, Article 103(2), Article 130(3), Article 132a and Article 147(1) of the Constitution;
3. the size of taxes, fees, and labour and social security payments and contributions;
4. the state budget;
5. the rules of the internal organisation and procedure of the National Assembly.
fix: (repealed)
items.why: Lifts the ban on referendums about taxes, the budget, parliament's rules and listed constitutional matters.

items.text: Codes and laws that comprehensively regulate a given field may not be put to referendum in their entirety.
items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Allows whole codes and comprehensive laws to be put to a referendum.

properties.explanation: If parliament is dissolved or its term ends before it decides on a petition, the petition lapses: the law does not say the procedure continues before the next parliament.

items.fix: If the term of office of the National Assembly ends, or it is dissolved, before it has decided on a petition submitted under Article 10(2), the procedure shall continue before the newly elected National Assembly, which shall decide on the petition within three months of its first sitting.
items.why: A petition no longer lapses when parliament dissolves or its term ends.

properties.explanation: Citizens cannot call a vote to overturn a decision once it has been adopted.

fix: (1) If, within 100 days of the promulgation of a law, an initiative committee submits a petition containing the signatures of no fewer than 50,000 citizens with voting rights, the law shall be put to a national referendum.
(2) The law shall not enter into force before the referendum. It shall be deemed rejected if more than half of the voters taking part in the referendum have voted “no”.
items.why: Lets citizens call a vote on any new law before it takes effect.

properties.explanation: The law does not require any decision to go to a vote automatically.

items.fix: Laws amending the Constitution, and decisions to ratify international treaties that transfer powers of the State, shall enter into force only after their approval by national referendum.
items.why: Sends the most fundamental decisions to the voters automatically.

properties.explanation: Not met. Voters must first choose a party list, and a preference is optional. Only one preference is allowed, with no ranking as in the single transferable vote; a ballot with more than one counts for the list only. A vote without a preference counts as a preference for the first candidate on the list, which, together with the 7% threshold, makes it almost impossible to replace that candidate. In practice, only about 3% of members of parliament have been elected thanks to preference votes.

items.text: Elections for members of parliament are held under a proportional electoral system, with candidate lists of parties and coalitions, or of initiative committees, registered in multi-member constituencies.
items.fix: Elections for members of parliament are held under the single transferable vote, in multi-member constituencies of three to five seats.
items.why: Replaces party lists with the single transferable vote in districts of 3 to 5 seats.

items.fix: When voting, the voter may rank as many candidates as they wish in order of preference, by marking 1, 2, 3 and so on beside their names, regardless of the party, coalition or committee that nominated them.
items.why: Lets voters rank candidates of any party, instead of one preference within a list.

fix: The vote is valid if at least one candidate has been marked with the number 1.

items.fix: (repealed)
items.why: Ends the rule that gives unmarked preferences to the list's first candidate.

items.fix: Candidates are elected by the single transferable vote: each ballot counts for the voter's highest-ranked candidate who can still use it, and surplus and eliminated candidates' votes are transferred by the voters' next preferences until all seats are filled.
items.why: Replaces the 7% preference threshold with STV counting.

properties.explanation: 31 multi-member districts matching the regions (Sofia split in three, Plovdiv in two).

items.text: For the elections, the territory of the country is divided into 31 multi-member constituencies, including three in Sofia City and two in Plovdiv region. The other constituencies coincide with the boundaries of the regions of the country.
items.fix: For the elections, the territory of the country is divided into constituencies of three to five seats each, with about the same number of voters per seat, following the boundaries of municipalities and regions where possible.
items.why: Draws smaller districts of 3 to 5 seats, so each area has its own representatives.
